notes: Current AMD and Unsloth llama.cpp builds do not list TurboQuant KV cache types such as turbo4.
These profiles use q4_0 KV cache as the supported long-context memory-saving mode.
UD profiles use Unsloth Dynamic GGUF weight quants where available; they are not the same as upstream TurboQuant/TQ cache types.

Qwen3.8-27B is a hybrid Gated DeltaNet model: only 16 of its 64 layers hold a KV cache, so context is cheap and weights are the binding constraint. It needs llama.cpp b10419 or newer; the pinned b8407 does not know the architecture.
ubatch values in 65..256 collapse throughput by up to 40x on hybrid models. Never sweep inside that band.

qwen38-27b-iq4xs-sanity is the go/no-go gate: it runs with no offload at a short context purely to measure whether the Gated DeltaNet kernel is GPU-accelerated on gfx1201. If tg128 lands near CPU speed, the remaining qwen38 profiles are not worth running.

MTP draft depth is set for an offloaded split: speculation amortizes weight reads but not arithmetic, so on a CPU-resident portion the optimum is shallow (2-3) and depth 7 can be slower than no speculation. Sweep {0,2,3,5,7} and re-sweep after any change to the -ot pattern. See docs/TUNING.md section 1.1.
Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (Alibaba, Apache-2.0) is the authoritative reference for this family; every GGUF is a derived artifact and its publisher and revision must be recorded and verified separately.

The MTP head is blk.64. A GGUF that quantizes it to Q4_K measures 0% draft acceptance and speculation fails silently; Q5_K-Q8_0 reaches 73-74%. Verify with gguf-dump before benchmarking any qwen38 profile - the nominal quant label does not tell you.

cache_ram_mib is intentionally unset on the qwen38 profiles: context checkpoints are upstream-reported non-functional on hybrid/recurrent models, and the admission gate charges the cache to commit in full, so an inert cache costs headroom. Set it only after qwen38-27b-iq4xs-agentic-restore passes on the candidate runtime.

The qwen38-27b-buun-* profiles run on the pinned spiritbuun/buun-llama-cpp fork, which implements the hybrid/recurrent checkpoint correction the upstream profiles above cannot get. They are a candidate runtime under docs/adr/0010, not a replacement: the upstream baseline stays exactly as it is and remains the fallback.

cache_ram_mib is 0 and cache_idle_slots is false on every buun profile, stated rather than omitted. The fork ships cache_ram_mib=8192 and cache_idle_slots=true, so omitting either enables a host prompt cache the manifest never declared and admission never charged. This is a context-checkpoint experiment, not a prompt-cache experiment; the two are different mechanisms.

VBR, TurboQuant, TCQ and the fork's own KV types stay off for the first qualification. An explicit -ctk/-ctv q4_0 clears the fork's variable-bitrate alias, which is what keeps the KV format identical to the upstream control. Evaluate them later as a separate experiment against this configuration, never by editing it.

The buun profiles must be run against an upstream control at the same context, fixture and settings. Measure both with scripts/v2/Measure-V2AgenticReuse.ps1 and diff them with Compare-V2Runtimes.ps1, which refuses two reports whose control variables differ. A decode benchmark is not evidence for this question.

Everything about Qwen3.8-27B on buun-llama-cpp in this file is unverified on gfx1201. No profile here has been run; the checkpoint correction is verified at source level by cia-fork-gate and nothing more.

context_checkpoints.objective: The smallest checkpoint count that keeps incremental reuse consistent without a relevant re-prefill. Judge on processed-versus-new prompt tokens, reuse ratio, TTFT, prompt tokens/s, peak RAM and commit, checkpoint creation and invalidation counts, and memory stability across turns - together, not on any one of them.
context_checkpoints.note: Do not maximize the checkpoint count because host RAM allows it, and do not run the full grid blindly: eliminate a bad region from the first results and stop. A larger checkpoint count costs commit, which is this machine's binding constraint.

spec_draft_n_max.note: Confirm blk.64 is Q5_K or better with gguf-dump before sweeping; at Q4_K acceptance is 0% and the sweep measures nothing. Partial CPU offload moves the optimum down, so do not assume 7 wins - it can be slower than no speculation at all. Re-sweep after any change to the -ot pattern.

context_size.note: The target is functional capacity near 256k, not the round number. Draft acceptance collapses at particular context sizes on a ~2048-token period (llama.cpp #23658), so if a neighbouring value is substantially better, ship the better value.
